chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Imam is ahead of you by one rak'ah and you attain the final recitation, you recite in the third of his prayer, and it is the second for you; and if you do not attain with him except one rak'ah, you recite in it and in the one that follows it. And if he is ahead of you by one rak'ah, you sit in the second for you and the third for him, until the rows are equal in standing. He said, and he said: When you find the Imam prostrating, remain in your place until he raises his head; and if he is sitting, you sit; and if he is standing, you stand.

key_terms.الْقِرَاءَة: Recitation (specifically the Quranic recitation in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for joining the Imam late in prayer and aligning the rows?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* provides precise jurisprudential guidance for latecomers (*muqtadi*) joining the Imam, emphasizing the principle of following the Imam's actions even if it results in a temporary misalignment of rows. It clarifies the calculation of valid versus missed rak'ahs and mandates mirroring the Imam’s posture (standing, sitting, or prostrating) to maintain congregational unity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on strict adherence to the Imam's lead in communal worship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the Imam is ahead of you by one Rak’at and you attain the last recitation, you should recite (for yourself) in the third from his Salāt, and it would be the second for you; and if you do not attain with him except for one Rak’at, you should recite in it and in the one which follows it. And if he is ahead of you by one Rak’at, sit in the second one for you and it would be the third for him, until the rows are standing’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If the Imam is one Rak‘at ahead and you join in the last recitation, recite in the third Rak‘at for him which is the second for you. You must do so even if you cannot join him for more than one Rak‘at in which you recited as well as in the one that follows. If he is one Rak‘at ahead of you, sit down in the second Rak‘at for you and the third for him until the row stand up in line.’ He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) said, ‘If you find the Imam in Sajdah (prostration) remain where you are until he raises his head, and if he is sitting, you also sit down, and if he is standing, stand up.’”
